### [Developing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with our customers](https://www.anthropic.com/news/enterprise-frontier-safeguards)

**Anthropic** · 2026-09-01

Anthropic announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), combining zero data retention (ZDR) with misuse monitoring by storing data directly within customer-controlled cloud infrastructure.

- EFS addresses safety risks in Mythos-class models (like Claude Fable 5.1) by enabling long-term correlation of traffic across multiple sessions and accounts to detect cyberattacks and credential theft.
- Data is hosted within customer-managed cloud environments rather than Anthropic's infrastructure, solving compliance hurdles associated with standard 30-day data retention policies.
- Eligible enterprise customers will receive temporary ZDR on Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 pending the phased rollout of EFS starting later in fall 2026.
- Supported environments will include Claude Code, Claude Enterprise, Claude Platform, AWS (Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform), Google's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry.

**Why it matters:** It allows organizations in heavily regulated sectors like banking and healthcare to deploy advanced agentic AI models while satisfying strict regulatory privacy constraints.

### [Claude Fable 5.1 made me a really nice animated pelican](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/1/claude-fable-5-1/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-01

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, featuring a 52.6% score on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 and five variable reasoning effort levels ranging from low to max.

- Claude Fable 5.1 scores 52.6% on the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 benchmark, up from 24.7% for Fable 5 and 22.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol.
- Fable 5.1 features five reasoning effort settings: low, medium, high, xhigh, and max, with no option to disable reasoning entirely.
- At low and medium effort settings, Fable 5.1 skipped reasoning completely for an SVG generation prompt, using roughly 2,000 output tokens in ~23 seconds.
- Higher reasoning settings scale output tokens and cost significantly, reaching 36,767 tokens ($1.83, ~8 min) at xhigh and 65,927 tokens ($3.30, ~14 min) at max.

**Why it matters:** The model demonstrates significant advancements in scientific problem-solving while providing fine-grained control over computational cost and reasoning depth via variable effort settings.

### [datasette-mcp 0.2](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/1/datasette-mcp/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-01

datasette-mcp 0.2 is the first non-alpha release, updating execute_sql output formats and adding a minimum dependency on mcp>=2.1.1.

- Changed execute_sql 'rows' output from an array of arrays to an array of objects to help weaker models map column names to values.
- Added a strict dependency on mcp>=2.1.1.
- Marks the first stable, non-alpha release of the datasette-mcp plugin.

**Why it matters:** Structuring SQL row output as objects prevents LLMs from misidentifying column data by positional index during database queries.
